## Overview

LRPITT28 is the **site-adjusted available-case modified-ITT** analysis for letter-sound knowledge (YARC-LSK) (`yarclet`)—the site-robustness companion to LRPITT07. It adds study site (`area`: 1 = North, 2 = South; 30 / 24 children in the repository). Unlike the SES covariates, `area` is fully observed, so it causes no additional exclusion beyond the letter-sound analytic requirement; LRPITT28 and LRPITT07 use the same outcome-available rows. The estimand is the assigned-arm contrast in $L_{\text{post}}$ in that fitted sample. A causal reading requires archive, outcome and analytic-variable selection not to induce an association between assigned arm and potential outcomes; extending the result to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity.

_Identification and sign convention._ Under the locked causal DAG, $G$ is a randomised root, so the offer contrast in the original full randomised cohort requires no baseline-covariate adjustment. This fit instead conditions on archive inclusion and observed outcome and analytic variables; a causal reading of $\tau$ in the fitted sample requires that selection did not induce an association between assigned arm and potential outcomes, while extension to all 57 requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity. The own baseline, linear age and site term are **precision / robustness terms only** — they may sharpen $\tau$ and probe its stability but do not identify effects after selection. **Sign convention:** $G = 1$ is the intervention arm, so a **positive** $\tau$ means the intervention arm has the higher modelled outcome.

## Model

$$
\eta_i = \alpha + \tau\, G_i
       + \gamma_{\text{own}}\, \text{logit}_*(L_{\mathrm{pre},i}, N)
       + \gamma_A\, A_{\text{std},i} + \gamma_{\text{area}}\, z(\text{area}_i),
$$

with Beta-Binomial likelihood $L_{\text{post},i} \sim \text{BetaBinomial}(N, \mu_i\kappa, (1-\mu_i)\kappa)$,
$\mu_i = \sigma(\eta_i)$, $N = 32$. The site term enters as a linear $\gamma_{\text{area}}$
(the same weak $\text{Normal}(0, 0.3)$ prior as cross-baseline couplings); HSGPs are
off by default. Priors follow the shared template in `priors.py`.
